A University of Florida sorority sister died after being hit by a car Saturday night while crossing the street near her college campus – despite a bystander’s desperate efforts  to help her.

Hazel Krauss, 19, was struck at around 11:30 p.m. while she was crossing West University Avenue in Gainesville when the driver swerved to avoid hitting another vehicle, cops said.

Registered nurse Porchia Hardy saw Krauss and rushed to help, but the freshman student was later pronounced dead at hospital.

“I’m a mom, and a nurse, so my mom and nurse instincts kicked in, and I mean she was in good care,” Hardy told WCJB.

Krauss was a student at the University of Florida’s Warrington College of Business and a member of the Delta Gamma sorority, the outlet reported.

She had graduated from St. Ignatius College Prep in Chicago earlier this year and was a member of the girls’ volleyball and bowling teams and active in student clubs there, according to WLS.

“Hazel reflected the very best of what we hope to see in our graduates: a willingness to grow, intellectual curiosity, faith, love for others and a sincere commitment to justice,” Saint Ignatius College Prep said in a statement provided to the outlet.

“Through the joy she brought to her studies, athletics, faith and service, she made a lasting mark on her classmates and all who knew her.”

Gainesville Police Department said that their investigation into Krauss’ death was ongoing.

“According to the preliminary investigation, a vehicle was traveling eastbound on W. University Avenue when the driver swerved to avoid another vehicle,” police said.

“During the maneuver, the vehicle struck a 19-year-old female pedestrian who was crossing the roadway and collided with the other vehicle.

“A nurse at the scene assisted the pedestrian until EMS arrived. She was transported to UF Health Shands Hospital, where she later died from her injuries.”
